theory.intro: A **credit card** is a reducing balance loan: interest is charged on the amount currently owing, and every repayment lowers it. Interest is usually compounded **daily**, from and including the day of the purchase.
facts: The daily interest rate is the annual rate divided by $365$: $18.25\%$ p.a. gives $r = \dfrac{0.1825}{365}$.
Each purchase is its own compound interest calculation, $FV = PV(1+r)^{n}$, where $n$ is that purchase's own number of days.
Count the days as the question directs: from $8$ March to $31$ March inclusive is $31 - 8 + 1 = 24$ days.
The **closing balance** is the total owing on the statement date, so it is the sum of the grown amounts of all the purchases.
The interest charged is the closing balance minus the total of the purchases themselves.
An **interest-free period**, often $55$ days, applies only when the previous statement was paid in full.
The **minimum payment** is a small percentage of the closing balance, not the whole balance, so a debt repaid that way lasts a long time.
A **cash advance** is cash taken out on the card; it has no interest-free period and usually a higher rate.
Keep the full value in the calculator and round the money answer once, at the end.
steps: Write down the daily interest rate.
Count the number of days for each purchase.
Add the results and round the money answer once, at the end.

foundation.question_text:
A credit card charges interest at $21.9\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Find the daily interest rate, as a fraction and as a decimal.

A purchase is made on $14$ May and the statement is issued on $31$ May.
Interest is charged from and including the purchase date up to and including the statement date.
For how many days is interest charged?

A purchase of $\$640$ is made on a credit card with no interest-free period, charging $16.4\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Interest is charged for $25$ days.
Find the amount owing, to the nearest cent.

A purchase of $\$1250$ is made on a credit card with no interest-free period, charging $14.6\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Interest is charged for $30$ days.
Find the interest charged, to the nearest cent.

A credit card charges $14.6\%$ p.a. compounded daily with no interest-free period, from and including the purchase date to and including the statement date of $30$ April.
A purchase of $\$460$ is made on $22$ April and one of $\$180$ on $27$ April.
Find the closing balance, to the nearest cent.

A credit card statement shows a closing balance of $\$2480.60$.
The minimum payment is $2\%$ of the closing balance, or $\$30$, whichever is greater.
Find the minimum payment.
foundation.solution_text:
$2\%$ of the closing balance $= 0.02 \times 2480.60$
$= \$49.61$
Since $\$49.61 > \$30$, the minimum payment is $\$49.61$.

foundation.question_text:
Mia's credit card has a $55$-day interest-free period, which applies only when the previous statement was paid in full.
Mia paid her previous statement in full, then bought a television for $\$780$ and paid the new statement in full $40$ days later.
How much interest is she charged on the purchase?
foundation.solution_text:
The previous statement was paid in full, so the interest-free period applies.
The $\$780$ was repaid after $40$ days, which is inside the $55$-day interest-free period.
No interest is charged, so the interest is $\$0$.

foundation.question_text: Explain why a credit card is an example of a reducing balance loan, and state one way in which it is different from a home loan.
foundation.solution_text:
Interest on a credit card is charged on the amount currently owing, not on the amount first spent.
Each repayment lowers that balance, so the next interest charge is smaller — exactly how a reducing balance loan works.
A home loan has a fixed repayment each period, while a credit card only sets a minimum payment, so the amount repaid varies.

development.question_text:
A credit card charges $18.25\%$ p.a. compounded daily with no interest-free period, from and including the purchase date to and including the statement date of $31$ March.
A purchase of $\$840$ is made on $8$ March and one of $\$250$ on $19$ March.
Find the closing balance and the interest charged, to the nearest cent.

Jonah owes $\$900$ on a credit card charging $14.6\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Interest is charged for $20$ days, after which he repays $\$400$.
How much does he owe immediately after the repayment, to the nearest cent?

Rosa owes $\$1600$ on a credit card charging $21.9\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Interest is charged for $12$ days, after which she repays $\$650$.
How much does she owe immediately after the repayment, to the nearest cent?

A cash advance of $\$500$ is taken on a credit card at $25.55\%$ p.a. compounded daily.
Cash advances have no interest-free period, and interest is charged from and including the day of the advance.
Find the amount owing $40$ days later, to the nearest cent.

A credit card charges $21.9\%$ p.a. compounded daily with no interest-free period, from and including the purchase date to and including the statement date of $30$ June.
The June transactions are shown.
$\begin{array}{|l|l|r|}\hline \textbf{Date} & \textbf{Transaction} & \textbf{Amount} \\ \hline \text{6 June} & \text{Airline tickets} & \$500 \\ \hline \text{18 June} & \text{Car service} & \$300 \\ \hline \end{array}$
Find the interest charged for June, to the nearest cent.

Dev's credit card has a $55$-day interest-free period that applies only when the previous statement was paid in full.
Last month Dev paid only the minimum, so no interest-free period applies.
He makes a purchase of $\$620$ and interest at $18.25\%$ p.a. compounded daily is charged for $22$ days.
Find the interest charged, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
The previous statement was not paid in full, so interest runs from the purchase date.
$r = \dfrac{0.1825}{365} = 0.0005$, $n = 22$
$FV = 620(1.0005)^{22}$
$= \$626.86$
Interest $= 626.86 - 620$
$= \$6.86$

mastery.question_text:
A credit card charges $21.9\%$ p.a. compounded daily with no interest-free period, from and including the purchase date to and including the statement date of $31$ August.
The August transactions are shown.
$\begin{array}{|l|l|r|}\hline \textbf{Date} & \textbf{Transaction} & \textbf{Amount} \\ \hline \text{5 August} & \text{Furniture} & \$700 \\ \hline \text{17 August} & \text{Tyres} & \$400 \\ \hline \text{26 August} & \text{Groceries} & \$250 \\ \hline \end{array}$
The minimum payment is $3\%$ of the closing balance.
Find the closing balance, the interest charged and the minimum payment, each to the nearest cent.

A single purchase of $\$2000$ on a credit card compounding daily grew to $\$2012.03$ over $20$ days, with interest charged for all $20$ days.
The annual rate is one of $10.95\%$, $14.6\%$, $18.25\%$ or $21.9\%$.
Find the annual interest rate.

Priya's credit card statement shows a closing balance of $\$3200$, and the minimum payment is $2.5\%$ of the closing balance.
She pays only the minimum on $1$ October and makes no further purchases.
Interest at $21.9\%$ p.a. compounded daily is charged on the amount owing for the $31$ days of October.
How much does she owe at the end of October, to the nearest cent?
